tasks.label: yamt: run the merge window
tasks.detail: Start the merge window (just dev-web), then open http://localhost:5173 in GNOME Web. Running it again restarts it with the current code; an open page reloads itself. Stop it with Ctrl+C in its terminal.

tasks.label: golden: build conflict repo
tasks.detail: Rebuild one of the 10 real conflicts as a git repo in /tmp/yamt-<case>, to open it in WebStorm/PhpStorm.

tasks.label: merge: new conflict project
tasks.detail: Replace /tmp/yamt-conflict-project with a fresh repo in the middle of a merge: 7 conflicted files (text, CRLF, both added, binary, deleted on one side).

tasks.label: merge: open in WebStorm
tasks.detail: Open /tmp/yamt-conflict-project in WebStorm (made first if missing); then Git → Resolve Conflicts.

tasks.label: merge: open in yamt
tasks.detail: Build yamt (debug, pages built in) from the current code and open it on /tmp/yamt-conflict-project (made first if missing). Running it again closes the open yamt window and rebuilds. The terminal shows yamt's exit status when you close it.
tasks.command: test -d /tmp/yamt-conflict-project/.git || scripts/conflict-repo.sh /tmp/yamt-conflict-project; just app --repo /tmp/yamt-conflict-project; echo "yamt exit status: $?"

tasks.label: lsp: new conflict project
tasks.detail: Replace /tmp/yamt-lsp-project with a fresh repo in the middle of a merge: 2 conflicted .ts files in web/ (oxlint and TypeScript underline problems, oxfmt formats) and a conflicted api/stats.py (ruff underlines problems and formats). math.ts and stats.py each have problems and a badly formatted line outside the conflicts. Installs typescript-language-server and ruff once into ~/.cache/yamt (needs the network the first time), and adds ruff (.venv/bin/ruff server, for py and pyi) to your yamt settings' servers added by hand unless it is there.

tasks.label: lsp: open in yamt
tasks.detail: Build yamt (debug, pages built in) from the current code and open it on /tmp/yamt-lsp-project (made first if missing). The first time, yamt asks whether to start the project's language servers; the answer is kept for that folder (Settings → Language servers changes it). Ctrl+S formats with oxfmt (.ts) or ruff (.py), then saves. Running it again closes the open yamt window and rebuilds.
tasks.command: test -d /tmp/yamt-lsp-project/.git || scripts/lsp-repo.sh --servers /tmp/yamt-lsp-project; just app --repo /tmp/yamt-lsp-project; echo "yamt exit status: $?"

inputs.description: Real conflict to rebuild in /tmp for PhpStorm
